blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result
s: A cholesterol test can measure:

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result
s: total cholesterol – the overall amount of cholesterol in your blood

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result
s: good cholesterol (called HDL) – this may make you less likely to have heart problems or a stroke

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result
s: non-HDL cholesterol – the difference between total cholesterol and HDL

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result
s: When you get your result, you may just be told your total cholesterol.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result
s: You might be able to get separate results for your HDL and non-HDL cholesterol too.
Ask your doctor or nurse.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result > View your results online
s: Results of tests you had at your GP surgery, and results that have been shared with your GP surgery, may be available in your online GP health record.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > About your cholesterol result > View your results online
s: View test results in your GP health record

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > How your GP uses your results
s: Your GP will use your cholesterol levels along with other factors, such as your age, blood pressure and health conditions, to estimate your risk of cardiovascular disease.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > How your GP uses your results
s: They may give you a score (called a QRISK score) which estimates how likely you are to have a heart or circulation problem over the next 10 years.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be
s: What is a good target level for you depends on things like your age, whether you have any health conditions and your risk of cardiovascular disease.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be
s: These levels are a guide for healthy adults.
If you have been ill, are taking some medicines, or have recently had a baby, your levels may be lower or higher.
It does not make much difference to these levels whether you have eaten before your test or not.

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be
s: Result | Healthy level

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be
s: Total cholesterol | Below 5mmol/L

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be
s: HDL (good cholesterol) | Above 1.0mmol/L for men or above 1.2mmol/L for women

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be
s: Non-HDL (bad cholesterol) | Below 4mmol/L

blocks.path: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol > What your cholesterol levels should be > Further information
s: Find out more about cholesterol test results on the HEART UK website
